description:
## Problem
Only five cloud adapters cancel remote work on a run timeout (Onehouse Quanton, BigQuery, EMR Serverless, Glue, Dataproc). The survey in #4435 / docs/operations/run-safety.md lists adapters whose clients do offer cancel or stop but that were left without cleanup because they do not track what the run started: Athena and Athena Spark (stop query/calculation, terminate session), Databricks (cursor cancel), Snowflake (abort by query id), Starburst (cursor cancel), Synapse / Fabric Warehouse / Fabric Lakehouse (ODBC cancel), Fabric Spark and Synapse Spark (Livy statement cancel, delete a session the run created), ClickHouse Cloud (`KILL QUERY` by query id), Dataproc Serverless (no batch cancel in the Python client). Users on those platforms see the "BenchBox cannot cancel it on this platform" warning.

## Change
For each listed adapter, decide whether it can reliably record what this run started (statement/query/session ids at submission, not after completion). Where it can, implement `cancel_remote_work()` through the existing hook and `StartedRemoteWork`, set the manifest capability `run_timeout_cleanup`, and update the capability table. Where it cannot, record why in the table. Adapter SDK imports stay lazy.

## Decision gates
- Only stop what this run started; if an adapter cannot tell what it started from what pre-existed, implement nothing for it and say so in the table.
- Warnings use the two owner texts verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120).
- No live cloud run: stubbed clients only (live checks belong to run-timeout-remote-cleanup-live-check-20261122).

## Verification rubric
Per adapter implemented, a stubbed-client test that fails before: cancel/stop called for started work on timeout, never for pre-existing work, a failure reported without hiding exit 124. `make platform-manifest-check` and `make pr-preflight` exit 0; the updated table is in the pull request.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
